deviation: DEVIATION: X41 external-tool microprobe; not canonical and not a validation transfer

drake_probe.formulation: discrete MultibodyPlant hydroelastic contact, rigid sphere on compliant box

mujoco_reference.formulation: MuJoCo convex soft constraints, 5 mm-radius cylinder against the blind-hole floor under the validated insertion controller

metric_definitions.drake_penetration: sphere radius minus final sphere-center height above the undeformed plane
metric_definitions.drake_normal_impulse: sum(abs(hydroelastic spatial-force z))*0.0001 s over the 1.0 s simulation
metric_definitions.mujoco_penetration: max(0, -tip_z - plate_thickness) at the final episode sample
metric_definitions.mujoco_normal_impulse: sum(abs(contact_force_z))*0.0005 s over the full 16.3 s episode

caveat: These values are not apples-to-apples. Drake uses a user-selected volumetric hydroelastic modulus, a rigid sphere, gravity loading, and a 1 s horizon; MuJoCo uses convex soft constraints, a cylinder in the insertion fixture, controller loading, and a 16.3 s horizon. The 744 um versus 24.7 um penetration difference primarily demonstrates formulation and parameter dependence, not that either engine is more accurate.
rationale: Drake is cheaply available and can reproduce a stable 15 N contact, but a decision-quality insertion comparison would require calibrated hydroelastic material properties and a dedicated insertion model. X41 therefore records availability and the microprobe without adopting Drake as a replacement benchmark.
